nodes.name: Winter snow and frost
nodes.desc: Snowfall and hard frost shape the high plateau, and snowmelt feeds the streams and pools that supply water downstream.

nodes.name: Mountain streams and pools
nodes.desc: Headwater streams, pools and waterfalls of the plateau, part of a wider area that supplies fresh water to Lesotho, South Africa and Namibia.

nodes.name: Grassland fire
nodes.desc: Burning is a common feature of southern African mountain grassland and renews grass growth. General ecology.

nodes.name: Thin mountain soil
nodes.desc: Cold, high-altitude soils hold the nutrients that grasses and heath plants draw on.

nodes.name: Soil microbes and fungi
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants, dung and carcasses and return nutrients to the soil.

nodes.name: Goat-beard grass
nodes.desc: The most frequently recorded plant near the reserve, a tussock grass of the Afromontane grassland.

nodes.name: Red grass
nodes.desc: A widespread tussock grass of African grasslands, grazed by hoofed animals and adapted to periodic fire.

nodes.name: Top heath
nodes.desc: A heath shrub of the high Drakensberg, whose tubular flowers offer nectar to birds. Genus-level link.

nodes.name: Grey rhebok
nodes.desc: A woolly-coated antelope of grassy highlands, a browser that gets much of its water from its food.

nodes.name: Common eland
nodes.desc: Africa's largest antelope, which feeds on grasses and shrubs. Rarely recorded near the reserve.

nodes.name: Cape hyrax
nodes.desc: A rock-dwelling mammal that feeds on grasses and shrubs near its cliff shelters.

nodes.name: Malachite sunbird
nodes.desc: A long-tailed nectar-feeding bird that visits heaths and other flowering plants and also takes insects.

nodes.name: Cape weaver
nodes.desc: A seed and insect eating bird of southern African grassland and scrub, a regular prey of shrikes.

nodes.name: Vari's brown
nodes.desc: A grassland butterfly of the Drakensberg; browns of this group have grass-feeding caterpillars. General ecology.

nodes.name: Southern fiscal
nodes.desc: A shrike that impales prey on thorns; recorded eating birds, frogs and insects.

nodes.name: Rock kestrel
nodes.desc: A small falcon that hunts lizards and insects from cliffs and open ground.

nodes.name: Southern rock agama
nodes.desc: A rock-dwelling lizard that feeds mainly on insects and is prey for raptors.

nodes.name: Clicking stream frog
nodes.desc: A small frog of streams and wet grass that feeds on insects and is eaten by shrikes and snakes.

nodes.name: Rhombic skaapsteker
nodes.desc: A grassland snake that eats frogs, lizards and small mammals.

nodes.name: Black-headed heron
nodes.desc: A heron that hunts in open grassland and at water edges, eating frogs, reptiles and small animals.

nodes.name: Bearded vulture
nodes.desc: Scavenger living mostly on bone, which it drops from height to crack. Southern African population is small and near threatened.

nodes.name: Cape vulture
nodes.desc: A cliff-nesting scavenger that eats the soft tissue of carcasses and breeds in Lesotho. Endangered.

nodes.name: Jackal buzzard
nodes.desc: A mountain raptor that hunts small mammals, snakes and lizards, and eats carrion outside the breeding season.
